$comment: Single source of truth for the theme. scripts/build-tokens.js generates scss/_tokens.scss and the :root block in css/cambridge-tokens.css from this file — edit here, then `npm run build`.

ink.comment: Pantone 547. The dominant structural colour: body text, headings, primary buttons, nav text. Not an accent — this is the colour the page is built from.

inkDeep.comment: Hover/active shade of ink (primary button hover).

muted.comment: Secondary text. Darkened from a first pass (#5b7480) to clear WCAG AA (4.5:1) on both --bg and --surface.

fill.comment: Subtle fill for inputs, chips, quiet notices.

teal.comment: Pantone 326. The one accent colour — used at low density: a header rule, an active nav underline, a notice edge. Never a text or background fill by itself (fails AA both directions).

tealInk.comment: Darkened teal for hover text and for anything teal that needs to carry text-level contrast (AA-safe on --bg and --fill).

focus.comment: Focus ring colour — same as ink.

overlay.comment: The tint over a page behind a modal. Ink (19 56 68) at low alpha rather than neutral black, so the page dims into the same family as everything else here.

overlayBlur.comment: Blur radius behind a modal. Enough that body text stops being readable — the page should read as out of focus, not merely tinted — while its shapes stay recognisable enough to place the box in context.

shadowModal.comment: The only elevation in the theme, for a modal. Ink-deep (12 38 46) rather than black, which reads grey against these blue-greens. Two layers: a wide soft one for the lift, a tight one to seat the edge.

fontSans.comment: Cambridge's specified secondary face. Body text, UI chrome.

fontSerif.comment: Stand-in for Feijoa (Klim Type Foundry, no free web-embeddable licence). Headings and the wordmark only.

gutter.comment: The one horizontal breathing space between page content and the viewport edge. Every .cam-*-inner and .cam-container uses it, so header, hero, body and footer line up at every width.

widthPage.comment: Full-width band content: header, masthead, footer.

widthWide.comment: Wide content column: hero, dashboards, tables.

widthText.comment: Reading measure: prose, forms, narrow pages.

categoricalPalette.comment: The full six-colour Cambridge primary palette, for when you need more than three categories (e.g. a legend with 4-6 series). Not used by the base theme's own components.
